title: Make Cancel mean cancelled for a CSV import

blocks.text: Customers upload CSV files of contacts, and the import runs in the background: each chunk of the file is parsed, its rows are staged, and the staged rows appear in the customer's account when the import commits. A support ticket says: "I pressed Cancel because I picked the wrong file. The screen said the import was cancelled. An hour later, all 40,000 contacts were in my account."
`run(...)` already imports correctly. Finish the three `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/CsvImport.java`:

items: `parse(...)`: one chunk, which may take a while;
`mayCommit()`: the last word before the rows become visible.

blocks.text: When you're done, an import the user cancels commits nothing, whether the click arrives while it waits on the storage or just before it commits. About six lines in total.
The tests run imports on a real `ExecutorService` and cancel them through the `Future` that `start` returns.

cases.says: an import that nobody cancels stages every row in order and commits once
cancelling an import that is waiting on the storage ends it, rather than leaving it waiting
an import cancelled while waiting on the storage stages no further chunk and commits nothing
a cancel that arrives after the last chunk was parsed still keeps the rows from being committed

origin.section: Cancelling a Future Asks; the Task Decides

concepts: Future.cancel(true) interrupts the task's thread and marks the Future cancelled at once; whether the task stops before its side effect depends on its own checks, and cancel(false) never interrupts.
